title: bug: a task file written before reopenCount existed can never be un-archived: set_task_status and the board compute undefined + 1 for the ARCHIVED to BACKLOG/WORKING reopen and updateTask refuses the NaN with an uncoded "reopenCount must be a non-negative integer", because StateManager.load backfills priority and comments but not reopenCount (48 live ARCHIVED rows)
description:
Filed by defect hunt #15 (task-928a468d), lane 3 (state persistence: backward compatibility with existing .moe/ state files). Verified at HEAD d5431577 in a git-archive snapshot outside the shared checkout.

PROBLEM
- StateManager.load() backfills legacy task fields in memory (packages/moe-daemon/src/state/StateManager.ts:1066-1079): priority, comments, contextFetchedBy and stepsCompleted. It does not backfill reopenCount.
- An un-archive counts as a reopen and computes task.reopenCount + 1. That happens in set_task_status (src/tools/setTaskStatus.ts:249) and in the board drag (src/server/WebSocketServer.ts:622). REOPEN_TASK (src/state/taskStore.ts:816) does the same for DONE/REVIEW rows. With no reopenCount on disk, the result is NaN.
- taskStore.ts:486-488 refuses NaN with a plain Error, "reopenCount must be a non-negative integer". So the un-archive fails, uncoded, and the row stays ARCHIVED.
- A null reopenCount happens to work, because null + 1 is 1.
- createTask already defaults a missing count to 0 (taskStore.ts:338). load never does.

CONTRACT
- docs/MCP_SERVER.md:1649 (### moe.set_task_status): "`ARCHIVED → BACKLOG/WORKING` un-archives."
- docs/SCHEMA.md:488: `reopenCount: number`.
- Epic rail: "Fixes must be backward-compatible with existing .moe/ state files".

EVIDENCE
- Repro: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-928a468d/A/sideLeads.test.ts, case 1 ("legacy ARCHIVED row without reopenCount can be un-archived by a human"). Copy it into packages/moe-daemon/src/__hunt__/ of a d5431577 snapshot and run `npx vitest run src/__hunt__/sideLeads.test.ts -t "legacy ARCHIVED"`.
  - Expected: "error": null, "status": "BACKLOG"
  - Received: "error": "reopenCount must be a non-negative integer", "status": "ARCHIVED"
- Output: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-928a468d/A/sideLeads.vitest.txt
- Live exposure, from a read-only scan of .moe/tasks on 2026-11-03 at about 23:45Z:
  - 48 ARCHIVED rows have no reopenCount key, mostly the 2026-02 bug-* imports;
  - 10 more ARCHIVED rows have reopenCount null.
  - None of them is active, so the failure shows only when a human un-archives one.

FIX DIRECTION
- In load()'s task backfill loop, set reopenCount to 0 when it is not a non-negative integer (missing, null or anything else), beside the priority and comments backfills.
- This fixes every reopen path at once, and it touches no file an open row holds: setTaskStatus.ts is held by task-a133bd6a, and WebSocketServer.ts is named by the IDE rows.
- Like its siblings, the backfill is in memory only. The next write of the row persists it.

FILES
- packages/moe-daemon/src/state/StateManager.ts
- packages/moe-daemon/src/state/legacyTaskBackfill.test.ts (new)
- Docs: none. The fix restores the documented un-archive, so no contract changes.

Placement: no open row holds these files at filing time. setTaskStatus.test.ts is only run here, never edited, because task-a133bd6a (REVIEW) edits it.
definitionOfDone: Loading a task file with no reopenCount key, and one with reopenCount null, gives state.getTask(id).reopenCount === 0 for both (new test file packages/moe-daemon/src/state/legacyTaskBackfill.test.ts)
moe.set_task_status ARCHIVED to BACKLOG on such a loaded row succeeds and stores reopenCount 1 (same test file)
`cd packages/moe-daemon && npx vitest run src/state/legacyTaskBackfill.test.ts src/state/StateManager.test.ts src/tools/setTaskStatus.test.ts` passes, run in a snapshot outside the shared checkout

implementationPlan.description: Test first, then the fix (both files). (a) Create packages/moe-daemon/src/state/legacyTaskBackfill.test.ts with the Write tool from the dry-run-verified prototype /mnt/d/moe-scratch/plan-93e09a54/legacyTaskBackfill.test.ts (read it, then Write it; never cp it into the tree, the rail needs a TOOL witness). On a fresh .moe/ in os.tmpdir() it has 3 tests: (1) six ARCHIVED files in the live legacy shape (no reopenCount, definitionOfDone or taskRails keys) with reopenCount missing / null / -1 / 1.5 / '2' / 3 load as 0,0,0,0,0,3, and every file's bytes are unchanged after state.load(); (2, it.each) a row with no key, and one with null, un-archives through setTaskStatusTool ARCHIVED -> BACKLOG (reason 'revive', no workerId: the human path) to status BACKLOG, reopenCount 1, reopenReason 'revive', in memory and in the task file. Run it once before the fix: test 1 and the no-key case fail (that one throws 'reopenCount must be a non-negative integer' from taskStore.ts:488); the null case passes, because null + 1 is 1. (b) Fix StateManager.load()'s task backfill loop (packages/moe-daemon/src/state/StateManager.ts:1066-1080 at a5157059) with the Edit tool. After `if (!Array.isArray(task.comments)) updates.comments = [];` add `if (!Number.isInteger(task.reopenCount) || task.reopenCount < 0) updates.reopenCount = 0;`, under a 2-line comment saying why: a file written before reopenCount existed has no key or null, so default it as createTask does (taskStore.ts:338) and every reopen path's `reopenCount + 1` stays a number. Change the loop comment to 'Backfill priority, comments and reopenCount for existing tasks'. The exact diff is /mnt/d/moe-scratch/plan-93e09a54/fix.diff. Keep the backfill in memory only, like its siblings: load() must never write the file, or the next daemon start rewrites 58 .moe/tasks files (test 1 pins the bytes); the row's next real write persists the value. Do not touch setTaskStatus.ts, WebSocketServer.ts, taskStore.ts or qaReject.ts. Every reopen site (setTaskStatus.ts:248, WebSocketServer.ts:622, taskStore.ts:816, qaReject.ts:188) reads the backfilled value. The FileWatcher reload (index.ts:821-830) calls state.load(), so an externally restored legacy file is covered too. Error handling: the default never throws and adds no IO. It runs inside load()'s existing try block, and updateTask's non-negative-integer check (taskStore.ts:486-488) stays unchanged as the backstop for a bad caller value.

Adversarial self-review of the 2-file diff (about +4/-1 in StateManager.ts, plus the new test). Check:
(a) Twice concurrently: the FileWatcher can re-run load() while a reopen is in flight. The default is idempotent and keeps a valid count, so a reload cannot reset a count that a reopen just wrote.
(b) Hostile inputs: missing, null, negative, fractional, string, NaN and Infinity all become 0.
(c) Assumptions: readers that already treat a missing value as 0 (getCommitScope.ts:288, metrics.ts:99, contextNextAction.ts:31) see no change. No test expects reopenCount to be undefined after load; step 2's full suite proves it.
(d) load() makes no writes: test 1 pins the bytes.
(e) No docs change: docs/MCP_SERVER.md:1649 (ARCHIVED -> BACKLOG/WORKING un-archives) and docs/SCHEMA.md:488 (reopenCount: number) already describe the restored behavior.
Confirm that the diff names exactly the two planned files and that both are declared (complete_step modifiedFiles).

executionContract.intendedBehavior: A task file that predates reopenCount loads with reopenCount 0, in memory only. That covers a file with no key, a null, or any value that is not a non-negative integer. Every reopen path (set_task_status, the board's /ws drag, REOPEN_TASK, qa_reject) then computes a number, so a human can un-archive the 48 legacy ARCHIVED rows (and the 10 with null). A valid count is kept unchanged. load() never rewrites a task file; the row's next real write persists the value.
acceptanceCriteria: Loading a task file with no reopenCount key, and one with reopenCount null, gives state.getTask(id).reopenCount === 0 for both; -1, 1.5 and '2' also load as 0, and 3 is kept (legacyTaskBackfill.test.ts)
set_task_status ARCHIVED -> BACKLOG on such a loaded row (human path, no workerId) succeeds and stores status BACKLOG and reopenCount 1, in memory and in the task file (same test file)
The task files' bytes are unchanged by state.load()
The checkRef passes: stage 1 is the DoD command over legacyTaskBackfill, StateManager and setTaskStatus tests, and stage 2 is the full daemon suite, run in a snapshot outside the shared checkout
invariants: updateTask still refuses a non-integer or negative reopenCount update (taskStore.ts:486-488 unchanged)
setTaskStatus.ts, WebSocketServer.ts, taskStore.ts and qaReject.ts are not edited; setTaskStatus.test.ts is only run
compatibility: Valid non-negative integer reopenCount values load unchanged

Backward-compatible with existing .moe/ state files (epic rail): no task file is rewritten at load. The default reaches disk only with the row's next real write, exactly like the priority and comments backfills
No MCP tool or wire contract change: docs/MCP_SERVER.md:1649 and docs/SCHEMA.md:488 already state the restored behavior
approvedScope: StateManager.load() task backfill loop (packages/moe-daemon/src/state/StateManager.ts:1066-1080 at a5157059): one reopenCount default and its loop comment
reuse: Reuses load()'s existing backfill loop: no new helper, and no per-site `?? 0` at the four reopen sites
sourceAssumptions: StateManager.load() (StateManager.ts:1064-1080 at a5157059) loads tasks with loadEntities and backfills priority, comments, contextFetchedBy and stepsCompleted in memory via this.tasks.set(id, { ...task, ...updates })
index.ts:821-830: the FileWatcher change callback reloads through state.load(), so the backfill also covers external edits

setTaskStatus.ts:221-248: isReopening (REVIEW/DONE/ARCHIVED -> WORKING/BACKLOG/PLANNING) sets updates.reopenCount = task.reopenCount + 1; WebSocketServer.ts:622, taskStore.ts:816 and qaReject.ts:188 add 1 the same way
Live scan of .moe/tasks on 2026-11-04: 48 files have no reopenCount key and 10 have null, all ARCHIVED; no other invalid values

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (a) `?? 0` at each `reopenCount + 1` site (setTaskStatus.ts:248, WebSocketServer.ts:622, taskStore.ts:816, qaReject.ts:188). Rejected: four files, two of them in other rows' lanes, and any future site repeats the bug. (b) Persist the backfill at load (a write per legacy row). Rejected: it would rewrite 58 .moe/tasks files on the next daemon start (board churn), and the sibling backfills are in memory only. (c) Chosen: one in-memory default in load()'s existing loop.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: load() is also the FileWatcher's reload path (index.ts:821-830), so one backfill covers both startup and external edits. updateTask validates only the update's own reopenCount (taskStore.ts:486), so a legacy row fails only when it is reopened. A null count already worked by accident (null + 1 is 1). Readers already default a missing count to 0 (getCommitScope.ts:288, metrics.ts:99, contextNextAction.ts:31).
planningNotes.risks: Do not write task files in load(); test 1 pins the bytes. Do not edit setTaskStatus.test.ts; it is only run. Prototype status: RED 2 failed | 1 passed; GREEN 3 DoD files 164/164; full suite 281 files, 7437 passed | 24 skipped; tsc clean. The gate dry-run and negative control were both run from a --shared clone at a5157059 with uncommitted edits.
